root_cause.text: The `l2cap_ecred_conn_req` function in the Bluetooth L2CAP subsystem calculates the response length (`rsp_len`) using an unvalidated command length (`cmd_len`) before verifying if the number of SCIDs exceeds `L2CAP_ECRED_MAX_CID`, causing an out-of-bounds read from a local stack buffer (`pdu`) when handling an invalid request.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows that the assignment `rsp_len = cmd_len;` was originally executed before the `if (num_scid > L2CAP_ECRED_MAX_CID)` check. Moving this assignment after the check ensures that if the check fails and jumps to the `response` label, `rsp_len` remains 0 instead of retaining the attacker-controlled oversized value, preventing `l2cap_send_cmd()` from reading past the 18-byte `pdu` buffer.

When receiving L2CAP_CREDIT_BASED_CONNECTION_REQ the remo
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 7cf3b1dd6aa603fd80969e9e7160becf1455a0eb
Author: Luiz Augusto von Dentz <luiz.von.dentz@intel.com>
Date:   Mon Mar 15 13:04:37 2021 -0700

    Bluetooth: L2CAP: Fix not checking for maximum number of DCID
    
    When receiving L2CAP_CREDIT_BASED_CONNECTION_REQ the remote may request
    more channels than allowed by the spec (10 octecs = 5 CIDs) so this
    checks if the number of channels is bigger than the maximum allowed and
    respond with an error.
    
    Signed-off-by: Luiz Aug
